text:
Anaheim arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, riding a three-game winning streak after a 5-4 win in Edmonton last night, and without A.J. Greer and Ryan Poehling. Calgary, rested by a day, lost 2-1 in overtime at Seattle two days ago and is 2-2-1 in its last five, missing Connor Zary and Samuel Honzek. The teams split their two October meetings, each side winning by two goals.

Our numbers see an even game (ANA 3.10 expected goals, CGY 3.12, meaning the quality of chances each should produce). The Ducks create more and give up more: 3.10 for and 3.48 against per 60 minutes, against 2.73 and 3.23 for the Flames. Calgary's record undersells it, since finishing and goaltending have cost them. In net, projected starters Lukas Dostal (+0.27 goals saved above expected this season, -3.71 last) and Dustin Wolf (-5.54, -2.80) both enter shaky, though Wolf's year has been rougher. The Ducks have also taken 5.4 penalties a game, and Calgary's power play is the weaker of the two units.

Cutter Gauthier leads the Ducks at 41% to score, on a six-game point streak. Leo Carlsson is one assist from 100 career assists and sits at 77% for a point. Joel Farabee tops the Flames at 30% to score. Among our under-the-radar picks, Judd Caulfield (20% to score) has produced 3.3 expected goals over his last 10 games on a third line, and Mikael Backlund is 48% for a point against a Ducks defense that allows a lot of chances.
